originalTitle: United Airlines experiencing a widespread system outage, airline says
content: A widespread, yet short-lived, system outage at United Airlines on Monday delayed some outbound flights at US airports, the airline told CNN in a statement, coming on the heels of a rare FAA ground stop that caused massive disruption. The outage lasted about 30 minutes, with fewer than 150 flights impacted, United Airlines spokesperson Leslie Scott told CNN. United acknowledged the issue just before 5 p.m. ET, saying the technology outage was impacting departing flights, and an hour later the airline announced it had been resolved. “While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights,” United Airlines said in a statement. During the incident, the FAA said United was experiencing a technology outage on its end and that “it’s not an FAA equipment issue.” United said there is no indication that the outage was a cybersecurity-related issue. The technology outage affected access to multiple applications used by flight crews, according to an internal company alert obtained by CNN. The airline instructed pilots not to log out of several systems, warning they may be unable to sign back in. The affected applications included flight planning, weather briefing and crew management tools. Pilots unable to access their flight plans were being directed to contact dispatchers to have the documents emailed to them. The memo did not disclose the cause of the outage. Air traffic control audio captured by ATC.com shows the moment the outage occurred. “Hey, we’re uh, still waiting on our final weights,” a pilot on United Flight 1728 in El Paso, heading to Denver, said to a controller. “We just contacted ops and apparently there’s a company-wide system outage on it so might be a while.” The controller responds back, “United 1728, roger, so you don’t have any idea when you think you’ll be able to leave?” “No ma’am,” the pilot responds. Aviation industry still recovering from weekend ground stop The industry had largely returned to normal operations after the nationwide ground stop was lifted just after 8 p.m. ET on Friday, though airlines have still worked to reposition planes, crews and luggage as they grappled with the weekend’s score of cancellations and delays. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy held a 45-minute news conference Saturday morning to address the FAA ground stop, and apologized to travelers as he said he was still working to determine what exactly went wrong. Duffy told reporters that upgrade work on an old telecommunication system could be a cause for Friday’s nationwide ground stop. In at least one remote FAA location, Duffy said contractor L3Harris was doing routine maintenance to switch telecommunication lines from an old copper wire to fiber, which he described as “straightforward” work that has been happening across the country for decades. As United Airlines indicated for Monday’s system outage, Friday’s ground stop didn’t appear to have been caused by a cyber attack or any “nefarious” activity, Duffy stressed at the news conference. “A lot of questions came in yesterday. ‘Was this a, a cyber attack? Did some foreign nation attack this network?’ And the answer to that is we don’t believe so,” Duffy said. This story has been updated with additional information.
chineseTitle: 航空公司表示，联合航空遭遇大范围系统中断
chineseContent: 美国联合航空公司在一份声明中告诉美国有线电视新闻网，周一，美国联合航空公司发生了大范围但短暂的系统中断，导致美国机场的一些出境航班延误，此前美国联邦航空局罕见地进行了一次地面停留，造成了大规模的干扰。联合航空发言人莱斯利·斯科特 (Leslie Scott) 告诉 CNN，此次停电持续了约 30 分钟，受影响的航班不到 150 架。曼联在下午 5 点前承认了这个问题。 ET 表示，技术中断影响了离港航班，一小时后，航空公司宣布问题已得到解决。美国联合航空在一份声明中表示：“虽然部分航班延误，但对正在进行的航班或联合快运航班没有影响。”事件期间，美国联邦航空局表示，美联航遇到了技术中断，“这不是联邦航空局的设备问题”。美联航表示，没有迹象表明此次故障是与网络安全相关的问题。根据 CNN 获得的公司内部警报，技术故障影响了机组人员使用的多个应用程序的访问。该航空公司指示飞行员不要退出多个系统，并警告他们可能无法重新登录。受影响的应用程序包括飞行计划、天气简报和机组管理工具。无法访问飞行计划的飞行员被指示联系调度员，将文件通过电子邮件发送给他们。备忘录没有透露停电原因。 ATC.com 捕获的空中交通管制音频显示了停电发生的那一刻。 “嘿，呃，我们仍在等待最终的重量，”在埃尔帕索飞往丹佛的美联航 1728 航班上的一名飞行员对管制员说道。 “我们刚刚联系了运营人员，显然全公司范围内出现了系统中断，所以可能会持续一段时间。”管制员回复：“United 1728，罗杰，s
